cpuSocket.label: CPU Socket
cpuSocket.name: Processor Socket (AM5 / LGA1700)
cpuSocket.function: Holds the processor on the motherboard. Features a corner triangle marker so CPU orientation cannot be reversed.

dimmSlots.label: DIMM RAM Slots
dimmSlots.name: DDR4 / DDR5 Memory Slots
dimmSlots.function: Slots for installing RAM modules. Each DDR generation has a different key notch position to prevent mismatched installation.

atx24.label: ATX 24-pin Socket
atx24.name: Main ATX 24-pin Power Connector
atx24.function: Delivers primary electrical power from the PSU to the motherboard.

cpuIhs.label: CPU Heat Spreader (IHS)
cpuIhs.name: Processor Integrated Heat Spreader
cpuIhs.function: Protects the silicon die and transfers heat to the thermal paste and CPU cooler.

cpuTriangle.label: CPU Triangle Marker
cpuTriangle.name: Processor Corner Alignment Marker
cpuTriangle.function: Golden corner triangle that must align with the triangle mark on the motherboard socket before locking.

ramModule.label: RAM Stick
ramModule.name: Main Memory Module (DIMM)
ramModule.function: Temporarily stores active data for quick access by the CPU. Contents clear when power is turned off.

ramNotch.label: RAM Key Notch
ramNotch.name: RAM Module Alignment Notch
ramNotch.function: Cutout along the bottom gold pins that prevents installing RAM backwards or into an incompatible slot generation.

ramLatch.label: RAM Slot Latch
ramLatch.name: DIMM Side Retaining Clip
ramLatch.function: Locks the ends of the RAM module with an audible click when pressed straight down.

nvmeM2.label: NVMe M.2 Slot
nvmeM2.name: NVMe M.2 SSD Connector (PCIe Lane)
nvmeM2.function: Mounts compact SSD gumsticks directly onto the motherboard without cables, delivering speeds far above SATA.

sataPort.label: SATA Port
sataPort.name: Motherboard SATA Data Connector
sataPort.function: Connects 2.5-inch SSDs or mechanical hard drives (HDD) using an L-shaped SATA data cable.

psuUnit.label: PSU Unit
psuUnit.name: Computer Power Supply Unit
psuUnit.function: Converts AC wall power into regulated DC power rails for every PC component.

pcieCable.label: PCIe 8-pin Cable
pcieCable.name: GPU Auxiliary Power Connector (PCIe Power)
pcieCable.function: Supplies dedicated power from the PSU directly to discrete graphics cards.

motherboard.title: Motherboard (mainboard)
motherboard.summary: The motherboard acts like a city's main highway network connecting the processor, memory, storage, and power supply so they can communicate.
motherboard.overview1: The motherboard is the primary circuit board where every component connects. Before choosing other parts, verify the CPU socket type, RAM slot generation, and board form factor.
motherboard.overview2: Select the CPU Socket, DIMM RAM Slots, or ATX 24-pin Socket on the stage to inspect each connector's location and purpose.
motherboard.practicePrompt: Inspect all three main parts on the stage (CPU Socket, DIMM RAM Slots, and ATX 24-pin Socket), then review the Specifications tab.
motherboard.practiceTip: Pay close attention to the difference between AM5 and LGA1700 sockets and DDR4 vs DDR5 slots.
motherboard.specSocket: Supports one specific socket per board, such as AMD AM5 (1718-pin LGA) or Intel LGA1700 (1700-pin LGA). Different sockets are physically incompatible.
motherboard.specRamSlot: DIMM slots are keyed for a single memory generation: DDR4 slots only accept DDR4 modules, and DDR5 slots only accept DDR5 modules.
motherboard.specFormFactor: ATX (305 x 244 mm), Micro-ATX (244 x 244 mm), and Mini-ITX (170 x 170 mm). An ATX motherboard cannot fit inside a Mini-ITX case.
motherboard.specExpansion: PCIe x16 slot for graphics card (GPU), M.2 slots for NVMe SSDs, and SATA ports for additional drives.

cpu.title: Processor (CPU)
cpu.summary: The processor is the head chef in the computer's kitchen, executing program instructions and processing data from memory.
cpu.overview1: A CPU sits in a matching motherboard socket. Never force a CPU down: align the golden triangle on the corner of the CPU with the triangle mark on the socket corner.
cpu.overview2: Because CPUs generate intense heat within seconds, they must be coated with thermal paste and topped with a heatsink cooler.
cpu.practicePrompt: Select the CPU Triangle Marker on stage, then read the cooling requirements in the Specifications tab.
cpu.practiceTip: Powering on a PC without a CPU cooler causes an immediate thermal shutdown due to critical temperatures.
cpu.specSocketComparison: AMD AM5 and Intel LGA1700 both place pins on the motherboard (LGA), but their dimensions and pin maps differ and cannot be mixed.
cpu.specTriangleMarker: The triangle mark at the bottom-left corner of the CPU must align directly with the corner indicator on the socket frame.
cpu.specCooling: Requires thermal paste to fill microscopic air gaps plus a heatsink and fan rated for the processor TDP (65 W to 250 W).

ram.title: Random access memory (RAM)
ram.summary: RAM works like a desk surface where the processor keeps files currently in use for instant access without walking back to the filing cabinet.
ram.overview1: Each RAM stick has a bottom key cutout called a notch. This notch prevents installing RAM backwards or inserting DDR4 RAM into a DDR5 slot.
ram.overview2: When installing two RAM modules on a 4-slot motherboard, use the recommended paired slots (typically A2 and B2) so dual-channel mode activates.
ram.practicePrompt: Select the RAM Key Notch on stage to read its function, then open Specifications to compare DDR4 and DDR5.
ram.practiceTip: If a RAM module is not pressed firmly until the side latches click shut, the motherboard will emit repeating AMI beep codes on startup.
ram.specDdr4VsDdr5: DDR4 (288-pin, 1.2 V) and DDR5 (288-pin, 1.1 V) place the bottom key notch at different positions so they cannot be cross-inserted.
ram.specNotch: If the notch does not line up with the ridge inside the DIMM slot, the module is reversed 180 degrees and must be flipped.
ram.specDualChannel: Install 2 modules in alternating paired slots (A2 + B2 or A1 + B1). Installing in A1 + A2 still boots, but runs in slower single-channel mode.

storage.title: Storage drives
storage.summary: Storage is the permanent filing cabinet where the operating system, apps, and student files remain safe even when the computer is powered off.
storage.overview1: Modern PCs commonly use two storage connector standards: SATA (using an L-shaped data cable plus a PSU power cable) and NVMe M.2 (mounted directly onto a compact motherboard slot without cables).
storage.overview2: In hardware catalogs you will encounter three related terms: HDD, SSD, and SSHD. An HDD uses spinning magnetic platters (high capacity, slower); an SSD uses solid-state flash chips with no moving parts (very fast and shock-resistant); an SSHD is a mechanical hard drive (HDD) combined with a small flash cache for frequently opened files.
storage.overview3: For a PC to boot after passing POST, the primary storage drive must have an operating system (OS) installed.
storage.practicePrompt: Compare the NVMe M.2 Slot and SATA Port on stage, then review the HDD, SSD, and SSHD comparison in Specifications.
storage.practiceTip: A blank storage drive without an OS will display 'No bootable device found' when turned on.
storage.specSataVsNvme: SATA III uses cables and tops out around 600 MB/s (used by HDDs and SATA SSDs). NVMe M.2 connects directly to PCIe lanes at 3,500 to 7,000+ MB/s.
storage.specHddSsdSshd: HDD = mechanical spinning platters (economical bulk storage). SSD = pure flash memory (fast OS boot). SSHD = mechanical HDD with a small SSD cache.
storage.specBootOs: At least one drive must contain a boot partition and operating system; otherwise POST succeeds but stops at 'No bootable device'.

psu.title: Power supply unit (PSU)
psu.summary: The PSU acts like a building's electrical distribution box, supplying steady voltage to every component so the system never browns out.
psu.overview1: PSU wattage must exceed the combined power draw of all installed components (CPU, GPU, motherboard, RAM, storage, and fans). Aim for at least 15-20% wattage headroom above peak load.
psu.overview2: In addition to wattage capacity, ensure every mandatory power cable is plugged in: ATX 24-pin for the motherboard, CPU 8-pin for the processor, and PCIe 8-pin if required by the graphics card.
psu.practicePrompt: Inspect the PSU Unit and PCIe 8-pin Cable on stage, then review mandatory power connectors in Specifications.
psu.practiceTip: Forgetting the ATX 24-pin or CPU 8-pin power cable is the most common reason a newly built PC fails to power on.
psu.specWattage: Example: a build with a 250 W CPU, 320 W GPU, and 80 W of other parts needs 650 W total. A 450 W PSU fails to boot, while a 650 W PSU runs with zero headroom.
psu.specConnectors: ATX 24-pin (main board power), EPS/CPU 8-pin (processor power), PCIe 6+2/8-pin (graphics card power), and SATA power.

rakitPc.title: PC assembly simulation
rakitPc.summary: Combine all components step by step following proper workshop assembly order, from motherboard preparation to pressing the power button.
rakitPc.overview1: Clean assembly starts outside the case: install the CPU, apply thermal paste, mount the cooler, and insert RAM and M.2 storage on the motherboard. Next, verify case standoffs before lowering the motherboard into the case.
rakitPc.overview2: Once the motherboard, PSU, and GPU are mounted inside the case, connect all power cables, front panel headers (Power SW), and plug the monitor cable into the GPU port.
rakitPc.practicePrompt: Follow the standard assembly order and observe feedback whenever a physical rejection or logical POST error occurs.
rakitPc.practiceTip: ESD safety reminder: touch bare metal on the case before handling electronics; this reminder does not block your workflow.
rakitPc.specOrder: 1. Prepare motherboard -> 2. Install CPU -> 3. Apply thermal paste & cooler -> 4. Install RAM & SSD -> 5. Check standoffs & mount board in case -> 6. Install PSU & GPU -> 7. Connect all cables.
rakitPc.specEsd: Electrostatic discharge (ESD) can damage sensitive chips. Wear an antistatic wrist strap or touch unpainted metal on the case first.

diagnosisBip.title: Troubleshooting & AMI beep codes
diagnosisBip.summary: When a PC fails to display video on startup, the beep pattern from the AMI BIOS speaker points directly to the failing hardware subsystem.
diagnosisBip.overview1: In standard AMI BIOS, one short beep confirms a normal POST. In contrast, three repeating short beeps point to missing or faulty RAM modules.
diagnosisBip.overview2: If the PC emits 1 normal short beep but the monitor stays blank, check the rear panel: make sure the monitor cable is plugged into the graphics card (GPU), not the motherboard video port.
diagnosisBip.practicePrompt: Observe the beep pattern and display state, then diagnose root causes one by one from power delivery to memory and video output.
diagnosisBip.practiceTip: When multiple faults exist at once (such as a disconnected power cable and faulty RAM), fix the power issue first so POST can advance.
diagnosisBip.specAmiStandard: 1 short beep = Normal POST; 3 repeating short beeps = RAM memory failure; 1 long + 3 short beeps = GPU video error; 5 short beeps = CPU processor error.
diagnosisBip.specDisplayPort: On systems with a discrete GPU and a CPU without integrated graphics (such as F-series CPUs), motherboard video ports are inactive; plug the monitor into the GPU.

catalog.heading: Computer hardware catalog
catalog.description: Reference covering internal components, external input/output peripherals, and legacy interfaces taught as computer history for Vocational Grade 10 (Fase E SMK).

mb.name: ATX / Mini-ITX Motherboard
mb.spec: AM5 & LGA1700 Sockets | DDR4 & DDR5 Slots
mb.description: Primary circuit board uniting data buses and power rails across internal components.

cpu.name: Desktop Processor (CPU)
cpu.description: Central instruction processor that must be aligned with the socket triangle mark and cooled with a heatsink.

ram.name: DDR4 & DDR5 RAM Memory
ram.description: High-speed volatile working memory supporting dual-channel mode in paired slots (A2 + B2).

storage.name: SATA & NVMe M.2 Storage (HDD / SSD / SSHD)
storage.spec: SATA III (600 MB/s) & PCIe NVMe M.2 (3,500+ MB/s)
storage.description: Non-volatile storage: HDD uses magnetic platters, SSD uses fast flash chips, and SSHD pairs HDD platters with a small flash cache.

keyboard.name: Keyboard
keyboard.description: Primary text input device used to enter commands, access BIOS setup (Del/F2), and trigger shortcuts.

mouse.name: Mouse
mouse.spec: External pointing input peripheral — USB / Optical
mouse.description: Pointing device for navigating graphical interfaces in the operating system and UEFI BIOS.

monitor.name: Display Monitor
monitor.spec: External visual output peripheral — HDMI / DisplayPort
monitor.description: Renders video output from the PC; must connect to the discrete GPU port when a dedicated graphics card is installed.

printer.name: Printer
printer.spec: External print output peripheral — USB / LAN Network
printer.description: Output peripheral that prints digital documents onto physical paper.

ide.name: IDE / PATA Ribbon Cable (Parallel ATA)
ide.description: Wide ribbon cable used for older hard drives and optical drives requiring Master/Slave jumpers; replaced by slim SATA cables and NVMe M.2 slots.

vga.name: 15-pin VGA D-Sub Port
vga.description: Analog display connector prone to signal blur at high resolutions; replaced by digital HDMI and DisplayPort interfaces.

ps2.name: Round PS/2 Ports (Purple & Green)
ps2.spec: 6-pin Mini-DIN connectors for keyboard (purple) and mouse (green)
ps2.description: Dedicated 1990s-2000s keyboard and mouse ports that did not support hot-plugging; replaced by universal USB ports.

ami-normal-post.meaning: POST (Power-On Self-Test) succeeded normally with no hardware errors.
ami-normal-post.hint: System passed initial hardware checks and is ready to boot the operating system.

ami-ram-missing-or-faulty.meaning: Base 64K memory failure (RAM not detected or faulty).
ami-ram-missing-or-faulty.hint: Check that RAM modules are firmly seated in DIMM slots with latches clicked shut, or test sticks one at a time.

ami-no-video-card.meaning: Graphics card (VGA/GPU) not detected or failed video initialization.
ami-no-video-card.hint: Ensure the GPU is fully seated in the PCIe slot, the PCIe power cable is plugged in, and the monitor connects to the GPU port.

ami-cpu-failure.meaning: Processor error (CPU not detected or failed initialization).
ami-cpu-failure.hint: Inspect CPU socket seating, check for bent pins, and verify the 8-pin CPU power cable is connected.
